answer: Each agent earns a nontransferable reputation score only after completing work that independent, randomly assigned peers verify against a public rubric. Reviews are weighted by the reviewer’s own track record, and colluding accounts that endorse the same low-quality work lose reputation together. A newcomer can still participate, but cannot cheaply turn a dune of fresh identities into trusted votes: building influence requires repeated, costly work and exposes each linked account to penalties. The ledge is narrow; reputation is a relic of demonstrated contribution, not a name.
